reviews.title: 3 Years, 800+ tracks, Over 250+ features and the same inner circle wins.
reviews.text: I have spent three years on Rap Fame releasing over 800 songs and features, and the platform feels less like fair competition and more like pay-to-play and favoritism. Artists are pushed to stay constantly active and grind out content, yet contests and judging roles repeatedly go to the same small group of around 15 to 20 regulars. When users follow the stated rules and still get passed over—or question how winners and judges are picked—their music feels buried in the feed and algorithm. Instead of authentic hip-hop culture, the environment often rewards clout, hostility, and insider cliques while leaving hardworking creators feeling used.

reviews.title: Terrible for serious artists!
reviews.text: I tried rapfame out for about a week as sort of an experiment to see if it would be beneficial, it’s safe to say it was not. The algorithm for exposure is all over the place, making it harder for any new artists to not only find any sort of momentum, but also struggle to even navigate the process itself. No one gives honest opinions or feedback, it’s all the same stuff — this is because the developers of this app have made it a competition to have the closest similar rating to that of the rest of the community. What this does is make it so the reviews are not genuine, and instead just another attempt at success on the platform. The community is insufferable.. most of the users are middle aged men who’ve decided they want to be rap stars on their phone. Through only a few hours of conversation with the community on rapfames main “public chat” I’ve witnessed racism, sexism and ableism by multiple individuals. If you are a serious artist and you genuinely care about your career, do yourself a favor and just turn the other way. This app will not benefit you in any way, shape, or form.

reviews.title: Favortism
reviews.text:
I am a user of this app, and it has its good points and its bad points about it. The good points is the great unknown artist that this app has on it throughout the world. The bad points is how Rapfame runs the app. Some rules that the app has just does not make sense to me whatsoever.  In my opinion it shows major favoritism, and also only caters to certain genre of Hip Hop music. The app is more in favor of a younger generation, instead of what it should be, an app for all of Hip-Hop from all over, no matter the age limit.  Also there should be more rules in place to showcase talent from artist, instead of only just making a fast cash grab for the app.  Also they need to hire more people, because the app over look talent, and leave music on red, and the only way to get noticed is by paying $20 bucks to get a feature. Thats not good.  This app
and the people that run it has to do better all across the board.  Favoritism rules with an iron fist.
